correctness.rationale: The displayed group-payoff offset m−(m/g)sum_e(lambda) is algebraically exact for every binary profile. Accumulation gives mr−(m/g)BB^T(lambda); strict positivity of the finite Fermi logistic derivative makes equality of conditional directed comparisons equivalent to constant offsets along every neighbor pair. Connectedness yields a global constant. Regularity BB^T1=gr1 and the quadratic identity v^TBB^Tv=||B^Tv||^2 give the necessary-and-sufficient incidence kernel. The graph class follows from v_i+v_j=0 on edges (odd cycles force v=0); the complete multipartite classification follows by varying one chosen vertex of each class. The spectral obstruction is the Laplacian Poincare inequality followed by the signless minimum-eigenvalue bound. The logistic derivative upper bound and explicit coupling give finite-horizon TV control. An extracted self-contained Python 3 script passed 1227 exact-rational/numeric checks covering all binary profiles on a four-cycle, triangle, and complete 3-partite uniform hypergraph; this is corroboration, not proof of arbitrary size. Boundaries include omega>0 finite, connected two-section, all group sizes g, all player incidence counts r, fixed factors, fixed exogenous comparison sampling.

originality.rationale: The primary Wang–Szolnoki 2022 full-text formulas and sections on homogeneous correspondence/heterogeneous divergence were examined, as were the main network payoff invariance paper by Luthi–Tomassini–Pestelacci and relevant heterogeneous public-goods work by Flores et al. and Bervoets–Makihara. They supply the model and general payoff-shift concepts but do not state the necessary-and-sufficient incidence-nullspace classification, the full pathwise Fermi equivalence for nonconstant factors, or the graph-bipartite/nonbipartite dichotomy. Published mathematical-record semantic searches using the source, aliases and implication formulations returned no covering result. The classical unsigned-incidence/signless-nullspace fact is recognized as prior mathematics and not claimed as new by itself; the claim is the exact model-specific dynamic classification. Publication-priority uncertainty remains and the self-review conclusion is not independent.

value.rationale: Wang–Szolnoki report behavior differences from heterogeneity, creating a natural gap: determine exactly which heterogeneity patterns can leave the full evolutionary stochastic process unchanged. The result is a complete classification for every finite regular uniform interaction hypergraph, with a sharp bipartite vs odd-cycle boundary for regular graphs, a nontrivial (g−1)-dimensional set of genuinely heterogeneous equivalent games on complete multipartite interaction groups, an all-horizons trajectory coupling, and a spectral quantitative obstruction away from equivalence. These are concrete model-independent-of-size structural and interpretive consequences, rather than a one-case simulation or a mere parameter rephrasing. Known incidence facts are used as proof ingredients, not asserted as inherently new. Scope limits and possible broader prior coverage are explicit.
